chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Musa, from Harun ibn Muslim, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him)

Regarding His saying: 'O you who have believed, be patient and vie in patience and compete in steadfastness and fear Allah that you may be successful.' He said: 'Be patient in performing the obligatory duties, strive against your enemy, and remain steadfast (waiting) for your expected Imam.'

key_terms.رَابِطُوا: Remain steadfast/guard (often in context of waiting or military readiness)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir interpret the command to 'be patient and strive' in Surah Al-Imran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) elucidates the tripartite command in Surah Al-Imran by grounding spiritual patience in the observance of Fard obligations, active striving (Jihad) against enemies, and the crucial eschatological duty of Rabita (steadfast connection) with the Awaited Imam. This interpretation underscores the Shia concept of 'Waiting for Deliverance' (Intizar al-Faraj) not as passive inactivity, but as an active state of spiritual and political readiness anchored in the Imam's presence. The hadith thus bridges individual piety with communal leadership, highlighting the Imam as the focal point of the believers' steadfastness.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (13) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa from Haroon bin Muslim from al-Qassim bin Orwa from Burayd bin Mo’awiya al-Ijli that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said when talking about the Qur’anic verse, “Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast.” “Be patient in offering the obligations, persevere before your enemies and wait for your expected imam.”
